text:
A: Hello. Can you hear me all right?
B: Yes.
A: Good. I'm Neil.
B: Claire.
A: Nice to meet you. Er, I don't know whether you found that puzzle task as odd as I did.
B: It was fine. Bit pointless, but fine.
A: Yes, I did wonder what they're measuring with it. Whether it's how we do on the puzzle or how we feel about it afterwards. I expect we'll find out at the end. Or not.
B: Probably not.
A: No. So, er, where are you calling from?
B: Ely.
A: Ah. Lovely cathedral.
B: It's a good building. I'm not into the church side of it, but the octagon's worth seeing.
A: I've only been the once. We drove over the fens to get there and I remember thinking how strange the landscape is. Everything's sort of below the road.
B: Yeah, it is. Most of it used to be water, so. They drained it in the seventeenth century, the Dutch did a lot of it, Vermuyden, and it's still shrinking, the peat. Some of the fields are lower than the rivers next to them. You walk along the Ouse and you're looking down at the farmland. It's quite unsettling once you notice it.
A: That's fascinating, actually. I had no idea about it shrinking.
B: There's a post at Holme Fen they drove in in the eighteen-fifties, level with the ground, and now it's about four metres sticking out.
A: Four metres. Good grief.
B: Yeah. I walk the dog out that way a lot.
A: I'm in Loughborough, so it's Charnwood for me. Hills, granite, old quarries. I do a lot of walking, and I'm interested in the industrial side, canals mostly. I take photographs of locks and that sort of thing.
B: Is that the photo behind you?
A: It is. One of mine, on the Grand Union. I'm quite pleased with that one. The last roll I got developed, half of it was overexposed, so it's not always a success.
B: Film?
A: Old Fuji. I'm a bit stubborn about it.
B: Fair enough. I'd rather that than someone's phone filters.
A: What do you do, if you don't mind me asking?
B: I'm a dinner lady. Midday supervisor. It fits round my son.
A: Right.
B: I've got a history of art degree, before you ask. I don't use it.
A: I wasn't going to ask, to be fair. But I did a history degree with the Open University in my forties, so I'm not going to judge anyone on what they do with one.
B: Why'd you do it?
A: Mostly because I wanted to. I'm a site manager at a packaging factory, maintenance and health and safety, so it had nothing to do with work. I just regretted not going at eighteen. Took me six years of evenings.
B: That's quite a lot of evenings.
A: My wife would agree with you.
B: Ha. Erm, do you ever go to galleries? You said you take photos.
A: Nottingham Contemporary now and then. I quite often come out not knowing what I've just looked at, but I sort of enjoy that.
B: That's the right attitude, honestly. Most people pretend. I go to Kettle's Yard on my own on weekday mornings. It's the only time it's quiet.
